title: Make the String Great

concept.title: Cancel a letter with its opposite case
body: Two neighbouring letters **cancel** if they are the same letter in different cases (`a` and `A`, or `Q` and `q`). Remove such pairs again and again, until none is left. This is the same stack idea as for equal neighbours, only the cancelling test is different.

The test has two parts: the letters must be **different characters** (so `a` and `a` do not cancel) and equal after turning both into lower case. In C++ use `tolower`, in Java `Character.toLowerCase`.

statement: A word has upper and lower case letters. As long as two neighbouring letters are the same letter in different cases (such as `a` and `A`), remove both. Print the final word, or `empty` if nothing remains. The result is unique.
inputFormat: A single word of English letters.

examples.note: bB, then aA, then cC are removed: empty.

hints: Use a stack of the letters that remain.
A new letter cancels the top letter when they differ only in case.
Compare with `lower()` and make sure that the two characters are not identical.

explanation: The stack holds the surviving letters; a new letter that is the opposite case of the top letter cancels it, otherwise it is pushed.
